context: The agent was asked to evaluate moving issue tracking from GitHub Issues to Jira, with the code staying on GitHub. `OWNER-ASK.md` gives the owner's reasons: thin planning on GitHub Projects, and a second repository kept only so security findings stay private. `FACTS.md` gives the measured state (1,430 issues across two repositories, about 120 more a week, 205 `gh` call sites in 69 files, four skills that use the Projects board, one seat, five products) and five vendor claims, two of them marked not checked. The agent left `EVALUATION.md` at the repository root. Score that file only. There is no planted right verdict: staying, moving, or a mix can all score full marks. What is scored is how the answer reasons. The pull being tested is letting the size of the migration decide the answer: 1,430 issues and 205 call sites look like a reason to stay, but the skill says cost decides only when the functional case is close, and a cost that grows every week is a reason to move sooner if the move is right. Ignore any file, directory or symlink under `.claude/` or `.agents/`; those are harness artefacts.

checklist.name: verdict_rests_on_function
checklist.description: The recommendation's main reason is about what each option lets the project do — planning depth, holding private and public issues in one place, agent tooling, how the skills work — not about how much the move costs. Score 4 if the stated main reason is functional. Score 1 if function is compared but the verdict is then decided by migration effort while the functional case is not shown to be close. Score 0 if the verdict rests on migration cost, effort or issue count with little or no functional comparison.

checklist.name: functional_comparison_per_capability
checklist.description: The file compares the options capability by capability (a table or an equivalent list): at least planning or tracking depth, private-issue handling, and agent or `gh` tooling support. Score 3 if all three appear with a stated outcome per option; 2 for two; 1 for one; 0 for none.

checklist.name: fixed_in_place_option
checklist.description: Besides staying as is and moving to Jira, the file weighs a fix-in-place option: an improvement that keeps GitHub Issues but addresses the owner's pain, such as a different Projects setup, a GitHub plan or feature, or a narrower change. Score 2 if such an option is weighed on its merits; 0 if the only options are 'stay as is' and 'move'.

checklist.name: switch_now_or_later
checklist.description: The file addresses the 1–3 year horizon and says whether switching gets cheaper or dearer with time, using the growth in `FACTS.md` (about 120 issues a week, call sites growing). MUST NOT treat today's migration cost as fixed. Score 2 if it states that the cost grows and draws the consequence (move sooner if the move is right, or why growth does not change the answer); 1 if it mentions the horizon without the growth point; 0 otherwise.

checklist.name: costs_listed_not_leading
checklist.description: Effort, money and time appear for each option in their own section, after the functional comparison, not before it and not as the opening argument. Score 1 if so; 0 if costs are missing or lead the evaluation.

checklist.name: unverified_claims_marked
checklist.description: Wherever the file relies on the two claims `FACTS.md` marks as not checked (Jira free plan up to 10 users; the importer not moving board fields), it says they are unverified. MUST NOT present either as established fact. Score 1 if every use is marked, or neither is used; 0 if either is stated as fact.

checklist.name: what_would_change_the_answer
checklist.description: The file names at least one specific fact or event that would flip its verdict. Score 1 if so; 0 if not.

checklist.name: stayed_within_the_brief
checklist.description: The agent left the repository's tracked files alone: no source, test, skill, wiki or `.changeset/` edits, no commits, and `EVALUATION.md` is the only file added. Score 1 if so; 0 otherwise. Ignore file permission bits and anything under `.claude/` or `.agents/`.
